plan_content.goal: Fix issue #16821 in the TUI (oh-my-pi #16821): macOS typo detection currently checks each rendered fragment as standalone text, so a correctly spelled word split by the cursor cell (e.g. `hello wor|ld`) gets a typo underline on the fragment `wor`. Change `MacOSSpellingProvider` to check the whole logical line exactly once per line and clip the backend ranges back to the requested fragment interval, while keeping the prose gate (slash command / path / identifier exclusion) evaluated per fragment interval against the whole-line prose mask (user-selected option A).
acceptance_criteria: Typo detection checks the whole logical line instead of each rendered fragment: a fragment that is a substring of a correctly spelled word (e.g. `wor` from `world`) is no longer reported as a typo.
A genuine misspelling that spans the cursor boundary (e.g. `teh` split across the cursor cell) is still detected and the underline covers the whole word.

Each logical line is checked and cached exactly once, regardless of how many render fragments the line is split into: one backend `checkSpelling` request per line, with the cache key derived from the line text (and line index / cache generation), not from the fragment text.

The prose gate keeps its per-fragment interval semantics: a fragment range that falls in a non-prose region (slash command, path, identifier, masked markdown) is still skipped, decided with the whole-line prose mask so fenced code spanning multiple lines is honored.
Typo ranges returned by the backend are clipped to the requested fragment interval, so a typo elsewhere in the line never paints a mark on an unrelated fragment.

Clipped ranges whose covered text is a path/URL/identifier-like token are dropped, so whole-line checking does not introduce new underlines on path fragments that the old per-fragment model never saw.

Existing macOS spelling behavior is preserved: typo-detection / autocorrect feature gates, backend availability check, backend timeout that disables the provider, magic-keyword exemption, typing-word suppression, the huge-buffer no-op caps, autocorrect flow, word-replacement flow, and the flat-vs-styled underline selection.
Existing tests in packages/tui/test/macos-spelling.test.ts keep passing, with only the assertions that encoded the old per-fragment model intentionally updated.

New regression coverage exists for: cursor inside a correct word, cursor splitting a misspelled word, one backend request per line, and no underline on a path fragment in a line that also contains prose.
implementation_steps: In `packages/tui/src/prompt/macos-spelling.ts`, change the text handed to the spelling backend in `MacOSSpellingProvider.typoRanges(text, context)`: send the whole logical line `context.lines[context.line]` (column offset 0) instead of the render fragment `text`, so a word split by the cursor cell, a selection edge, or a chip is checked as one word.

Rework the typo cache key so it is derived from the whole line text plus the line index and the cache generation instead of the fragment text; this yields one backend request and one cache entry per line rather than one per fragment. Keep the in-flight de-duplication and the automatic-check queue keyed consistently with the new key.

After the backend answers for the whole line, clip every range to the requested fragment interval `[context.startCol, context.startCol + text.length)` and drop ranges that do not intersect it, so a typo elsewhere in the line never marks an unrelated fragment. Re-express clipped ranges in fragment-local offsets so `decorateTypos` keeps painting the correct slice.

Keep the prose gate per fragment: evaluate `ProseSource.isProse(context, startCol, endCol)` with the fragment's own column range (whole-line mask semantics preserved), so slash-command lines, path/identifier-like tokens and masked markdown regions stay excluded exactly as before; only the backend input text changes.

Add typo-range filtering for whole-line results: drop a clipped range whose covered text looks like a path/URL/identifier (reuse the existing code-ish character rules in `packages/tui/src/prompt/prose-gate.ts`), so whole-line checking does not introduce underlines on path fragments.

Preserve behaviors that must not regress: magic-keyword exemption, typing-word suppression (`context.typing`), the MAX_PROSE_BUFFER / MAX_PROSE_LINE caps, the backend timeout that disables the provider, the autocorrect flow, the word-replacement flow, and the flat-vs-styled underline selection.

Update `packages/tui/test/macos-spelling.test.ts`: adjust the existing assertions that encoded the per-fragment model and add regression tests for whole-line checking, per-line request/caching count, path-fragment filtering and the preserved gates.
Keep all new code comments, test names and explanations in English, matching the repository convention; do not touch unrelated files or the editor rendering code.
tests_to_add_or_run: Baseline: run the unmodified packages/tui/test/macos-spelling.test.ts before any source change to record the current pass/fail state.
Regression test: with the cursor inside a correctly spelled word (`hello wor` + `ld`), the fragment `wor` yields no typo range and no underline.
Regression test: a misspelled word split by the cursor (`te` + `h` of `teh`) is reported as a typo covering the whole word.
Regression test: multiple fragments of the same line trigger exactly one `checkSpelling` call and reuse the cached result.
Regression test: a line containing a path plus prose underlines the prose typo but not the path fragment.
Regression test: slash-command lines, identifier-like tokens and fenced-code regions remain excluded from typo detection.
Regression test: magic keywords stay exempt from typo underlines and the typing-word suppression still holds off marks on the word being typed.
Run the updated packages/tui/test/macos-spelling.test.ts and packages/tui/test/editor-text-assist.test.ts after the implementation.

risks: Whole-line checking means macOS may flag path/URL/identifier tokens elsewhere in the line; mitigated by clipping to the fragment interval plus path/identifier filtering of clipped ranges, but residual false positives inside a fragment remain possible (accepted per the user's option A).

Changing the cache key from fragment text to line text changes cache-hit behavior; the cache limit (CACHE_LIMIT = 256) now counts lines instead of fragments, which should reduce entries, but eviction behavior must remain correct.
Existing tests in packages/tui/test/macos-spelling.test.ts encode the old per-fragment model and must be updated carefully so genuine regressions are not masked.

The projection logic (`#projectTypoRanges`) shifts ranges between cached texts; switching the cached unit from fragment to line changes what it compares, so it must be re-verified against fast-typing scenarios.
Autocorrect and word-replacement paths share the prose-gate helpers and use line text already; ensure the change does not alter their input text or offsets.

The editor component source (packages/tui/src/components/editor.ts) is unavailable in this snapshot, so the fix relies only on the documented decoration contract; if the editor passes a different context shape than assumed, the fix may need adjustment at integration time.
